question: What is the difference between automatic and manual offset commits?
options: Auto-commit periodically commits offsets in the background; manual commit lets the application control exactly when offsets are committed
Auto-commit stores offsets on disk; manual commit stores them in memory
Auto-commit works only for producers; manual commit only for consumers
There is no functional difference
explanation: With enable.auto.commit=true, the consumer commits offsets on a timer automatically. Manual committing (commitSync/commitAsync) gives the application precise control, which is important for processing guarantees.

question: Why can auto-commit lead to message loss with at-least-once expectations?
options: Because it commits offsets twice for each message
Because offsets may be committed before the records are fully processed, so a crash skips unprocessed records
Because it deletes messages from the broker after committing
Because it resets offsets to zero on every poll
explanation: Auto-commit can commit offsets for records that were fetched but not yet fully processed. If the consumer crashes after the commit but before processing, those records are skipped on restart, causing loss.

question: During a consumer group rebalance, what happens to partition assignments?
options: All partitions are deleted and recreated
The topic's replication factor changes
Partitions are revoked from consumers and reassigned among the current group members
Offsets are permanently reset to the earliest value
explanation: A rebalance revokes partitions from consumers and redistributes them among the active members according to the assignment strategy, ensuring each partition is owned by exactly one consumer.

question: What is the main advantage of incremental cooperative rebalancing over the older eager (stop-the-world) protocol?
options: It eliminates the need to commit offsets
It increases the replication factor automatically
It removes partitions from the topic
It avoids revoking all partitions at once, so consumers keep processing partitions they retain
explanation: Cooperative rebalancing only reassigns the partitions that actually need to move, letting consumers keep processing their unchanged partitions. This reduces the disruptive stop-the-world pause of the eager protocol.

question: To achieve at-least-once processing, when should a consumer commit offsets?
options: After the records have been successfully processed
Immediately after fetching, before any processing
Only once when the application starts
Never; offsets are irrelevant
explanation: Committing offsets only after successful processing ensures that if the consumer crashes, unprocessed records are re-read, giving at-least-once semantics (records processed at least once, possibly duplicated).
